correctness.rationale: Exact OU half-steps and a symmetric random rotation individually preserve the standard Gaussian and are self-adjoint in its L2 space, hence their symmetric composition is reversible and invariant. For shared noises, the difference is D R_theta D e. Gaussian trigonometric averages yield the exact symmetric 2x2 matrix; its Perron eigenvalue is the stated closed formula. Positive entries ensure sharpness. Entrywise monotonicity in r proves the sharp lambda->0 supremum; positive-probability strict contraction of coordinate basis vectors gives rho(h,0)<1. Matrix expansion gives 3-sqrt(5), and Cauchy-Schwarz yields the uniform W2 squared bound. The independent quadrature checker passed 466 checks; finite tests are auxiliary.

value.rationale: The 2026 motivating work makes a discrete convergence analysis a specific outstanding issue and uses a symmetric numerical splitting. For its most natural anisotropic Gaussian testbed, this finding supplies an exact, stable, bias-free, reversible discretization with a sharp all-step squared-coupling rate and an explicit uniform-in-condition-number W2 bound. The exact Perron constant permits step/anisotropy comparisons and distinguishes discrete quantitative robustness from merely continuous-time acceleration; it is not just a generic invariant-subflow argument.
